title: Your Busy Heart
blurb: It is as big as your fist and it never takes a day off. Meet the pump that keeps you alive.

chapters.title: A Pump the Size of a Fist
chapters.text:
Put your hand on your chest, a little to the left of the middle. Can you feel a gentle thump, thump, thump? That is your heart at work. If you have just been running, you will feel it more easily.

The heart is a strong muscle. It is about the size of your own fist, and it grows as you grow. Its job is to pump blood around your body. Blood carries oxygen and food to every part of you, from your brain to your toes. On the way back, it collects waste that your body needs to get rid of.

Your arm muscles can stop and rest for as long as you like. Your heart cannot. It starts beating before you are born, and it keeps going every second of your life, day and night. Its only rest is a tiny pause between one beat and the next. A child's heart beats about seventy to one hundred times a minute. That adds up to more than one hundred thousand beats a day.

You can stop your breath for a moment, but you can never tell your heart to stop. It works by itself. High up on the right side of your heart is a tiny patch of special cells. This patch sends out a small electrical signal, again and again, and each signal tells the heart muscle to squeeze.

So your heart keeps its own time, and you can think about other things.

questions.prompt: Where should you put your hand to feel your heart?
options: On your neck, just under your right ear
On your stomach, just above your belly button
On your back, between your two shoulders
On your chest, a little to the left of the middle
questions.why: The first sentence tells you to put your hand on your chest, a little to the left of the middle.

questions.prompt: How big is your heart?
options: About the size of a small coin
About the size of a football
About the size of your own fist
About the size of your whole head
questions.why: It is about the size of your own fist.

questions.prompt: What does blood carry to every part of you?
options: Oxygen and food
Waste and salt
Air and bones
Light and sound
questions.why: Blood carries oxygen and food to every part of you.

questions.prompt: How is your heart different from your arm muscles?
options: It gets its food from a different body
It cannot stop for a long rest
It is not really a muscle at all
It works only while you are awake
questions.why: Your arm muscles can rest for as long as you like. Your heart's only rest is a tiny pause between beats.

questions.prompt: About how many times does a child's heart beat in a day?
options: More than one hundred million times
About one thousand times
More than one hundred thousand times
About seventy times
questions.why: The text says that adds up to more than one hundred thousand beats a day.

questions.prompt: What tells the heart muscle to squeeze?
options: A small electrical signal from special cells
A message that you send when you decide to
The food that the blood brings to the heart
The air that comes in when you breathe
questions.why: A tiny patch of special cells sends out a small electrical signal, and each signal tells the heart muscle to squeeze.

questions.prompt: Why can you read a book without thinking about your heartbeat?
options: Reading makes your heart beat much more quietly
Your heart keeps its own time without your help
Your brain cannot think about two things at once
Your heart stops beating while you are sitting still
questions.why: The text says it works by itself and keeps its own time, so you can think about other things.

chapters.title: Four Rooms
chapters.text:
Inside, your heart has four spaces called chambers. You can think of them as four little rooms, two upstairs and two downstairs. The two upper chambers are called atria, and they collect blood. The two lower ones are called ventricles, and they are the strong pumps.

A wall in the middle divides the heart into a left side and a right side. The right side receives blood that has travelled around your body and has used up much of its oxygen. It sends this blood to the lungs to pick up fresh oxygen. The left side receives the fresh blood from the lungs and pumps it out to the rest of the body. That is a long trip, all the way to your toes and back, so the left ventricle has the thickest wall of all.

So your heart is really two pumps, side by side. Blood goes from your body to the right side, then to the lungs, then to the left side, and then out to your body again.

Small doors called valves open and close between the chambers. They make sure that the blood flows in only one direction. When doctors listen to your chest, they hear two sounds, over and over: lub-dub, lub-dub. Those sounds are the valves snapping shut.

Doctors listen with a tool called a stethoscope. A French doctor called René Laennec had the first idea for it in 1816. He rolled some paper into a tube, put one end to a patient's chest, and found that he could hear the heart clearly.

questions.prompt: What are the two lower chambers of the heart called?
options: Valves
Lungs
Ventricles
Atria
questions.why: The two lower ones are called ventricles.

questions.prompt: If a valve did not close properly, what would probably happen?
options: Some blood would flow back the wrong way
The lungs would fill up with fresh air
The blood would stop carrying any oxygen
The heart would grow two more chambers
questions.why: Valves make sure that the blood flows in only one direction. A valve that does not close could not stop blood going backwards.

questions.prompt: Where does the right side of the heart send blood?
options: To the toes
To the brain
To the stomach
To the lungs
questions.why: The right side sends this blood to the lungs to pick up fresh oxygen.

questions.prompt: Why does the left ventricle have the thickest wall?
options: It must stop the blood from getting back to the lungs
It pumps blood on the long trip around the whole body
It is the part of the heart that is nearest to the ribs
It has to hold more blood than all the other rooms
questions.why: The left side pumps blood out to the rest of the body. The text calls that a long trip, so the left ventricle has the thickest wall.

questions.prompt: Which list shows the path of the blood in the right order?
options: Lungs, right side, body, left side, lungs
Body, lungs, right side, left side, body
Body, right side, lungs, left side, body
Body, left side, lungs, right side, body
questions.why: Blood goes from your body to the right side, then to the lungs, then to the left side, and then out to your body again.

questions.prompt: What is the job of the valves?
options: To keep blood flowing in only one direction
To divide the heart into left and right
To make the blood pick up more oxygen
To send the electrical signal to the muscle
questions.why: They make sure that the blood flows in only one direction.

questions.prompt: What makes the lub-dub sound?
options: The wall in the middle shaking
The valves snapping shut
The blood hitting the ribs
The lungs filling with air
questions.why: Those sounds are the valves snapping shut.

questions.prompt: What did René Laennec use to listen to a patient's heart in 1816?
options: A hollow metal bell
A long rubber pipe
A wooden drum
A tube of rolled paper
questions.why: He rolled some paper into a tube and put one end to a patient's chest.

chapters.title: Roads for Blood
chapters.text:
Blood does not float around freely. It travels inside tubes called blood vessels, in the same way that cars stay on roads. If you stretched all your blood vessels in one line, they would be many thousands of kilometres long.

There are three main kinds. Arteries carry blood away from the heart. They have thick, stretchy walls because the blood inside them is under pressure. The biggest artery, called the aorta, leaves the top of the heart like a main road leaving a city.

Veins carry blood back to the heart. The blood in them flows more gently, and many veins have tiny valves to stop it slipping back as it climbs up from your feet. You may see some veins as blue lines inside your wrist. They only look blue because of the way light passes through your skin. The blood inside them is dark red.

Capillaries are the thinnest vessels, thinner than a hair. They link arteries and veins and pass oxygen to the cells. They are so narrow that red blood cells must go through them in single file.

Blood looks like a plain red liquid, but it is full of tiny working parts. Red blood cells carry oxygen. White blood cells fight germs. Tiny pieces called platelets help a cut to stop bleeding.

It takes about one minute for a drop of blood to travel all the way around your body and return to your heart.

questions.prompt: Why does the text compare blood vessels with roads?
options: Blood travels along them, as cars travel along a road
They are many different colours, like road signs
They carry only one kind of traffic at a time
They are as wide as roads in a large city
questions.why: Blood travels inside blood vessels, in the same way that cars stay on roads.

questions.prompt: Which vessels carry blood away from the heart?
options: Valves
Arteries
Capillaries
Veins
questions.why: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.

questions.prompt: Why do arteries have thick, stretchy walls?
options: They have to stay warm in cold weather
They must carry oxygen through to the skin
The blood inside them is under pressure
They need to stop the white cells escaping
questions.why: They have thick, stretchy walls because the blood inside them is under pressure.

questions.prompt: What is the aorta?
options: A kind of valve
A thin capillary
The smallest vein
The biggest artery
questions.why: The biggest artery is called the aorta.

questions.prompt: What stops blood slipping back in the veins?
options: White blood cells
Tiny valves
Thick walls
Platelets
questions.why: Many veins have tiny valves to stop it slipping back as it climbs up from your feet.

questions.prompt: What colour is the blood in a vein that looks blue?
options: Dark red
Almost white
Pale blue
Bright green
questions.why: They only look blue because of the way light passes through your skin. The blood inside them is dark red.

questions.prompt: Why must red blood cells go through capillaries in single file?
options: Capillaries are so long
The cells are carrying waste
The cells are in a hurry
Capillaries are so narrow
questions.why: They are so narrow that red blood cells must go through them in single file.

questions.prompt: A person's small cut takes a very long time to stop bleeding. Which part of the blood may be low?
options: Red blood cells
White blood cells
Platelets
Oxygen
questions.why: The text says tiny pieces called platelets help a cut to stop bleeding, so too few of them could make bleeding last longer.

chapters.title: Feel Your Pulse
chapters.text:
Every time the heart squeezes, it pushes blood into the arteries and makes them stretch a little. You can feel this stretch as a pulse. The easiest places are your wrist and your neck.

Try it now. Place two fingers on the inside of your wrist, below your thumb. Press gently, because pressing too hard can squash the artery so that you feel nothing. Do not use your thumb itself, because it has a pulse of its own. Count the beats for fifteen seconds and multiply by four. This gives your heart rate for one minute. If you count eighteen beats, your heart rate is seventy-two beats a minute.

When you are resting, a child's heart usually beats about seventy to one hundred times a minute. Other animals are very different. A mouse's heart can beat more than five hundred times a minute. A blue whale's heart can beat fewer than ten times a minute during a deep dive.

When you run or jump, your muscles need more oxygen, so the heart beats faster. Your heart also speeds up when you feel frightened or excited. It slows down again while you sleep.

You can test this for yourself. Measure your pulse while you are sitting still. Then do thirty star jumps and measure it again straight away. Keep checking every minute. Your heart rate will fall back towards where it started, and a fit person's heart usually gets there sooner.

questions.prompt: What are you feeling when you take your pulse?
options: Your lungs filling up with a breath of air
An artery stretching as blood is pushed into it
A small muscle moving inside your wrist
Your bones moving when your heart beats
questions.why: Every squeeze pushes blood into the arteries and makes them stretch a little. You can feel this stretch as a pulse.

questions.prompt: Why should you press gently when you take a pulse?
options: Pressing too hard can squash the artery
Pressing too hard can make your thumb hurt
Pressing too hard can make the count too fast
Pressing too hard can make the heart stop
questions.why: Press gently, because pressing too hard can squash the artery so that you feel nothing.

questions.prompt: Why should you not use your thumb to feel a pulse?
options: It moves too much when you count
It is too big to fit on the wrist
It has a pulse of its own
It is too cold to feel anything
questions.why: Do not use your thumb itself, because it has a pulse of its own.

questions.prompt: You count twenty beats in fifteen seconds. What is your heart rate for one minute?
options: Thirty-five beats a minute
Sixty beats a minute
One hundred beats a minute
Eighty beats a minute
questions.why: Count for fifteen seconds and multiply by four. Twenty times four is eighty.

questions.prompt: What does the text suggest about the heart rates of animals?
options: A huge animal needs a much faster heart than a tiny one
A tiny animal can have a much faster heart than a huge one
Only animals that live in the sea have slow heart rates
All animals have about the same heart rate as a child
questions.why: A mouse's heart can beat more than five hundred times a minute, and a blue whale's can beat fewer than ten times a minute.

questions.prompt: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?
options: Your heart gets much smaller
Your blood gets much heavier
Your muscles need more oxygen
Your lungs stop working for a while
questions.why: When you run or jump, your muscles need more oxygen, so the heart beats faster.

questions.prompt: When else does the text say your heart speeds up?
options: When you sit still to read a book
When you lie down and go to sleep
When you press on your wrist
When you feel frightened or excited
questions.why: Your heart also speeds up when you feel frightened or excited.

questions.prompt: What will you probably find if you keep checking your pulse after star jumps?
options: It falls back towards where it started
It stays exactly the same as it was at the end
It stops and starts again after one minute
It keeps on rising for the rest of the day
questions.why: The text says your heart rate will fall back towards where it started.

chapters.title: A Happy Heart
chapters.text:
You can look after your heart every day. The first rule is to move. Running, swimming, cycling and playing football make your heart stronger, just as lifting heavy things makes your arms stronger. A stronger heart pumps more blood with each beat, so it does not need to beat so often when you are resting. Doctors say children should be active for about an hour every day. That can be walking to school, skipping, climbing or dancing, and it all counts.

The second rule is to eat well. Fruit, vegetables, fish, nuts and whole grains keep the vessels healthy. Too much sugar and too much oil are not good for them. Over many years, fatty material can build up inside the arteries and make them narrower, as mud narrows a stream.

The third rule is to sleep. While you rest, your heart slows down and your body can repair itself. Children of your age need about nine to twelve hours each night.

Finally, never smoke, and keep away from smoke. It harms the heart and the lungs. If someone is smoking near you, it is fine to move away.

If you ever feel a pain in your chest, or your heart races when you have not been active, tell an adult. Most of the time it is nothing serious, but a doctor can check.

If you follow these rules, your busy heart will work hard for you for a very long time. By the time a person is eighty, their heart may have beaten about three billion times.

questions.prompt: What does regular exercise do for your heart?
options: It makes your heart stop more often
It makes your heart stronger
It makes your heart work by itself
It makes your heart smaller
questions.why: Running, swimming, cycling and playing football make your heart stronger.

questions.prompt: Why does a stronger heart not need to beat so often at rest?
options: It uses less blood than a weak heart
It has fewer chambers to fill up
It pumps more blood with each beat
It sends fewer signals to the brain
questions.why: A stronger heart pumps more blood with each beat, so it does not need to beat so often when you are resting.

questions.prompt: Which of these would count towards your hour of activity?
options: Walking to school
Watching a football match
Reading on the sofa
Sleeping for nine hours
questions.why: The text says walking to school, skipping, climbing or dancing all count.

questions.prompt: What can fatty material do to arteries over many years?
options: Make them stretchier
Make them turn blue
Make them longer
Make them narrower
questions.why: Over many years, fatty material can build up inside the arteries and make them narrower.

questions.prompt: About how many hours of sleep do children of your age need each night?
options: Six to seven
Three to five
Thirteen to fifteen
Nine to twelve
questions.why: Children of your age need about nine to twelve hours each night.

questions.prompt: Why does the text compare a narrow artery with a stream full of mud?
options: Both can be cleaned by drinking more water
Both have less room for the flow to pass through
Both carry water that is too dirty to drink
Both are found in the same part of the body
questions.why: Mud narrows a stream, and fatty material narrows an artery. In both, there is less room for what is flowing.

questions.prompt: What should you do if your heart races when you have not been active?
options: Hold your breath for a minute
Run faster to slow it down
Tell an adult
Wait and tell nobody
questions.why: If your heart races when you have not been active, the text says to tell an adult.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of this chapter?
options: A few daily habits help to keep your heart healthy
Only doctors can do anything about a person's heart
Your heart is healthy only when you are running fast
Children's hearts do not need any care until they grow up
questions.why: The chapter gives rules about moving, eating, sleeping and avoiding smoke, and says they help your heart for a very long time.
